descriptionChirho: The active Qal sense of physically sowing seed in the ground for agriculture, including literal field-sowing and the positive metaphorical extension of 'planting' people in a land (Arabic زَرَعَ zara'a, Korean 심다/뿌리다 simda/ppurida, Swahili -panda, Hindi बोना bona, Spanish sembrar).

Passive forms (Nifal, Pual, Qal Passive Participle) indicating land or seed that is sown or has been sown, describing fields or territory in a state of cultivation (Arabic تُزْرَعُ tuzra'u / مَزْرُوعَة mazru'a, Korean 뿌려지다 ppuryeojida, Swahili -pandwa, Hindi बोया जाना boya jana, Spanish ser sembrado).

Hifil causative participle describing plants that produce or bear seed, as in Genesis 1:11-12 'herb yielding seed' (Arabic يُزْرِعُ yuzri'u Form IV causative, Korean 뿌리는 ppurinun, Swahili -zaa 'bear fruit/produce', Hindi बीज देने वाला bij dene vala, Spanish que hace semilla).

Figurative Hifil and Nifal usage of 'sowing' applied to human conception: a woman 'producing seed' or 'being sown' meaning to conceive offspring, confirmed by Arabic حَبِلَ habila 'conceive' (NOT زَرَعَ), Korean 잉태하다/임신하다 ingtaehada/imsinhada 'conceive', Swahili -pata mimba 'become pregnant', Hindi गर्भवती होना garbhavati hona, Spanish concebir.

Metaphorical Qal usage of 'sowing' people among the nations meaning to scatter or disperse them, as in Zechariah 10:9, confirmed by Korean 흐트리다 heuteurida 'scatter' (NOT 심다 'plant'), Swahili -tawanya 'scatter/disperse' (NOT -panda 'sow'), Arabic وَأَزْرَعُهُمْ with pronominal suffix referring to people, Spanish sembrar used metaphorically.
